statement: The frozen v1 exact-eight parallel supervisor enforces one absolute build-work deadline on all active children even when finishing another already-exited child incurs a permitted blocking cleanup delay.

scope.description: Only build_20260930_exact_eight_parallel_batch.py SHA6b1b4c4f80a24e6851643032689df37a5a9641ee4c465ae04aab3f008ae8ec44 and its hard-work-deadline guarantee under the admitted blocking finish semantics. No mathematical encoding or research result is implicated.

assumptions: The supervisor uses the default single scheduler and calls child.finish(False) before its next deadline check.
A finished child cleanup can block for five seconds, as permitted by the frozen WindowsChild.finish wait bounds.
The second child remains active until cancellation; monotonic time advances during cleanup.
method: Independent deterministic clock/two-child countercontrol invoking the exact frozen supervisor; paired zero-delay positive. No production or Windows timing inference.
source_spec_basis: One absolute monotonic deadline starts at invocation entry and includes input checks and preparation; no deadline is reset per case.
Reaching it stops all new launches and terminates every active job.
The120 seconds is the maximum build-work deadline, with cleanup after that separately allowed.
shared_components: The actual frozen supervise function is the tested object. The clock and child lifecycle implementation are independently authored.
limitations: Simulation counterexample under an explicitly supported blocking-cleanup schedule; not an observed Windows runtime or performance benchmark.
No formula build, native solver, ledger or Git mutation occurred.
The shared-deadline guarantee is refuted; separate finite Job Object containment controls can still pass.
The metadata binding does not assert any user-facing scientific claim is invalid.
